Studies in patients with malaria1 and in healthy subjects2 indicate that the acute cardiovascular toxicity that may be associated with parenteral use of chloroquine is re- lated to transiently high plasma concentrations produced during the early part of the distribution phase; these findings appear to confirm that the dosage rate is a major determinant of this toxic- ity.
